subject: TrueCap #14 — small multi-family (5-12 units): different math
preheader: Commercial pricing kicks in · Cap-rate vs DSCR drives everything · The under-$1M sweet spot

marketSnapshot.headline: Fed week: rate cut likely Wednesday, what it means
marketSnapshot.body: Fed meets Wednesday — futures pricing in 90% odds of at least a 25bp cut, with 55% probability of 50bp. Either way, the actual cut has been substantially priced in over the last month (30Y already down to 6.45%) so don't expect another big leg lower on the announcement itself. The real signal will be the press conference language about pace of cuts through year-end. If Powell hints at more cuts in October/December, expect rates to break into the 6.20s. If he signals 'one and done,' rates stick around 6.4-6.5%.

dealSpotter.body: $725,000 for a 6-unit at $7,150/mo gross. 5+ units = commercial financing (different from residential 1-4). DSCR-style pricing typically 25-30% down at 7.5-8.0% rates. The math advantage: commercial buyers price these on cap rate compression, which means strong NOI improvement (raise rents 5%, upgrade laundry, sub-meter utilities) directly compounds the exit value. A 100bp cap-rate compression on an 8% cap property is roughly $90k of value creation on this deal.

$1.05M for an 8-unit at $10,200/mo gross. Below the $1M loan amount where pricing gets slightly worse, so use a community/regional bank that does sub-$1.5M commercial. Bloomfield rents have been moving +4-6%/yr; the under-management opportunity (current owner is 78 and has under-rented vs market for years) is real.

dealSpotter.headlineNumber: 9.1% cap · BUT one unit is tenant-from-hell
dealSpotter.body: $485k 5-unit. Four units are well-tenanted at market rents. The 5th has a long-term tenant who's been there 9 years, paying $400/mo when market is $1,150. Owner has been afraid to evict. Honest assessment: that unit's tenant is the deal. If you can get them out via cash-for-keys ($3-5k) or wait out the lease, you unlock $750/mo upside which is worth ~$100k of value. If they won't move, you've inherited the problem.

blogFeature.title: DSCR loans explained: rates, requirements, and when they make sense
blogFeature.excerpt: DSCR loans qualify the property, not you. For small multi-family deals where DTI doesn't pencil conventional, DSCR is often the path forward — but the trade-off is rate and ratio requirements that need to factor into your offer math.

qa.question: Is 5-12 units actually a better entry point than building up from single-family?
qa.answer: Depends on your starting point. The case for going straight to small multi-family: economies of scale on management (one PM relationship for 8 units vs eight relationships for 8 SFRs), value-add upside on under-managed properties (most 5-12 unit owners are not professional operators), and commercial pricing on cap-rate compression. The case against: bigger capital requirement (typically $200-400k down on a $1M deal), commercial financing is harder for first-timers without W-2 income or property-management track record, and the asset class has different operational rhythms (commercial lenders want you to have a property-management background or hire a credentialed PM). Practical answer: most investors should do 1-3 SFRs first to learn the operational side, then jump to small multi-family for property #4-6. The smaller-scale learning curve on a $200k SFR is much less painful than on a $1M 6-unit.
